Texas property tax for Amarillo homeowners is due by January 31 of the year after the tax year, and the 2026 bill is due Monday, February 1, 2027. Amarillo's city rate is $0.4307 per $100 of taxable value for 2025. Your full bill adds the county, the school district and any special districts to the city's share. This guide covers who bills you, the penalty schedule, ways to lower the bill and what to do if you want to sell with taxes owed.

Amarillo property tax: who sets it and who bills it

The Texas Comptroller says Texas has no state property tax. A county appraisal district sets your value, and each local taxing unit adopts its own rate. Amarillo lies in more than one county (Potter County, Randall County), so the county tax office that bills you depends on where the house sits.

The city's rate is $0.4307 per $100 of taxable value for 2025, according to the source below. We did not find the 2026 city rate on an official page.

  • Appraisal district: Potter-Randall Appraisal District.
  • We could not confirm from an opened official page which office collects the city's tax, so ask the city or the county tax office before you pay.

Due dates, penalties and liens

Texas property tax is due January 31 (Tax Code Sec. 31.02), and when that date falls on a weekend the deadline moves to the next business day (Sec. 1.06). Delinquent tax carries penalty and interest of 7 percent in February, 9 percent in March, 11 percent in April, 13 percent in May, 15 percent in June and 18 percent in July (Sec. 33.01), and an attorney collection fee of up to 20 percent can apply to accounts still unpaid on July 1 (Sec. 33.07).

A tax lien attaches to the property every January 1, and the owner on that date is personally liable for that year's tax, even if the house is sold later (Secs. 32.01 and 32.07). Read the full Texas property tax guide.

Penalty and interest grow every month after January 31. A cash sale can pay them off at closing, and you keep the rest.

Lowering a Amarillo tax bill

The residence homestead exemption takes $140,000 off the value for school district taxes, and homeowners who are 65 or older or disabled get an additional $60,000 (Tax Code Sec. 11.13). See the homestead exemption guide.

To protest your appraisal, file written notice by May 15 or 30 days after the notice was delivered, whichever is later (Sec. 41.44). See the protest guide.

How to sell a house in Texas when you owe tax in Amarillo

  1. Ask the tax office for the amount due in the month you expect to close, including any penalty, interest and attorney fee if the account is delinquent.
  2. Give that figure to the title company. Taxes are paid from the sale proceeds at closing, ahead of what you take home.
  3. Compare offers on what you actually net after taxes, repairs, commissions and closing costs.
  4. If time matters, ask for a written cash offer with a closing date you choose. We buy houses as-is, with no repairs and no agent commission. See how we buy houses in Texas.

What a cash sale of a Amarillo house looks like, step by step

People often ask what actually happens after they contact a cash buyer. Here is the usual order of events for a house in Amarillo.

  1. Tell us about the property. Use the form on this page or call or text (424) 435-2326. We ask about the address, the condition and what is going on, such as a mortgage, back taxes, tenants or an estate.
  2. Get a written cash offer. We review the details and send a written offer. There is no obligation, and you can turn it down and owe us nothing.

  5. You receive the proceeds. Our offers carry no agent commission, no fees and no closing costs to you.

Documents and information to have ready

You do not need everything below to get an offer, but each item makes the sale smoother and helps the title company work faster.

  • The deed or other proof of who owns the property today.
  • A recent mortgage statement or a payoff figure from the lender.
  • The latest property tax bill, plus any notice of unpaid or delinquent tax.
  • Homeowners association details, including dues and any unpaid assessments, if there is an association.
  • Current leases and the tenants' contact information, if the house is rented.
  • Estate paperwork, such as letters from the court, if you inherited the house.
  • A short list of known repairs. We buy as-is, but honest information avoids surprises.

Listing with an agent can bring a higher headline price when a house is in good shape and you have time. You pay the commission agreed in your listing contract, and you usually handle repairs, showings and the buyer's inspection requests. Closing depends on the buyer's financing.

Selling it yourself saves the listing commission but puts the marketing, the paperwork and the required Texas disclosures on you. You still need a title company or attorney to close.

Taking a cash offer trades some of the headline price for speed and certainty. We buy as-is, so there are no repairs, no showings and no financing contingency. It tends to fit owners dealing with foreclosure pressure, an inherited house, back taxes, tenants or a move on a deadline.   • Ask your lender for a written payoff figure good through your expected closing date, and ask whether there is a prepayment penalty.

  • If the house was inherited, ask the title company which court documents it needs before it will insure the sale.
  • If tenants live in the house, check the lease for its end date and any notice you must give.

You choose the closing date within what the title company needs to clear ownership and payoffs.

No. We buy houses as-is, so you do not need to make repairs before selling.

Tell us the payoff figure. A sale that does not cover the loan may need lender approval, so ask your lender about a short sale before you sign anything.

7 percent in February, rising to 18 percent by July, plus up to 20 percent in attorney fees after June 30 (Secs. 33.01 and 33.07).

Pearland property tax: who sets it and who bills it

The Texas Comptroller says Texas has no state property tax. A county appraisal district sets your value, and each local taxing unit adopts its own rate. We do not state a city rate here. The city page shows a current rate with no tax year, so we do not state a rate.

  • Appraisal district: Brazoria Central Appraisal District.
  • We could not confirm from an opened official page which office collects the city's tax, so ask the city or the county tax office before you pay.

Due dates, penalties and liens

Texas property tax is due January 31 (Tax Code Sec. 31.02), and when that date falls on a weekend the deadline moves to the next business day (Sec. 1.06). Delinquent tax carries penalty and interest of 7 percent in February, 9 percent in March, 11 percent in April, 13 percent in May, 15 percent in June and 18 percent in July (Sec. 33.01), and an attorney collection fee of up to 20 percent can apply to accounts still unpaid on July 1 (Sec. 33.07).

Penalty and interest grow every month after January 31. A cash sale can pay them off at closing, and you keep the rest.

Lowering a Pearland tax bill

The residence homestead exemption takes $140,000 off the value for school district taxes, and homeowners who are 65 or older or disabled get an additional $60,000 (Tax Code Sec. 11.13). See the homestead exemption guide.

To protest your appraisal, file written notice by May 15 or 30 days after the notice was delivered, whichever is later (Sec. 41.44). See the protest guide.

How to sell a house in Texas when you owe tax in Pearland

  1. Ask the tax office for the amount due in the month you expect to close, including any penalty, interest and attorney fee if the account is delinquent.
  2. Give that figure to the title company. Taxes are paid from the sale proceeds at closing, ahead of what you take home.
  3. Compare offers on what you actually net after taxes, repairs, commissions and closing costs.
  4. If time matters, ask for a written cash offer with a closing date you choose. We buy houses as-is, with no repairs and no agent commission. See how we buy houses in Texas.

What a cash sale of a Pearland house looks like, step by step

People often ask what actually happens after they contact a cash buyer. Here is the usual order of events for a house in Pearland.

  1. Tell us about the property. Use the form on this page or call or text (424) 435-2326. We ask about the address, the condition and what is going on, such as a mortgage, back taxes, tenants or an estate.

  5. You receive the proceeds. Our offers carry no agent commission, no fees and no closing costs to you.

  • The deed or other proof of who owns the property today.
  • A recent mortgage statement or a payoff figure from the lender.
  • The latest property tax bill, plus any notice of unpaid or delinquent tax.
  • Homeowners association details, including dues and any unpaid assessments, if there is an association.
  • Current leases and the tenants' contact information, if the house is rented.
  • Estate paperwork, such as letters from the court, if you inherited the house.
  • A short list of known repairs. We buy as-is, but honest information avoids surprises.

Listing with an agent can bring a higher headline price when a house is in good shape and you have time. You pay the commission agreed in your listing contract, and you usually handle repairs, showings and the buyer's inspection requests. Closing depends on the buyer's financing.

Selling it yourself saves the listing commission but puts the marketing, the paperwork and the required Texas disclosures on you. You still need a title company or attorney to close.

Taking a cash offer trades some of the headline price for speed and certainty. We buy as-is, so there are no repairs, no showings and no financing contingency. It tends to fit owners dealing with foreclosure pressure, an inherited house, back taxes, tenants or a move on a deadline. Compare every option on what you net after repairs, fees and carrying costs, not on the headline price.

  • Ask your lender for a written payoff figure good through your expected closing date, and ask whether there is a prepayment penalty.

  • If the house was inherited, ask the title company which court documents it needs before it will insure the sale.
  • If tenants live in the house, check the lease for its end date and any notice you must give.

You choose the closing date within what the title company needs to clear ownership and payoffs.

No. We buy houses as-is, so you do not need to make repairs before selling.

Yes. We buy rentals as-is, occupied or vacant. Tell us about the lease when you request an offer.

Tell us the payoff figure. A sale that does not cover the loan may need lender approval, so ask your lender about a short sale before you sign anything.

It depends on who has legal authority to sign. The title company can tell you what court paperwork it needs.

  • A recent mortgage statement or a payoff figure from the lender.
  • The latest property tax bill, plus any notice of unpaid or delinquent tax.
  • Homeowners association details, including dues and any unpaid assessments, if there is an association.
  • Current leases and the tenants' contact information, if the house is rented.
  • Estate paperwork, such as letters from the court, if you inherited the house.
  • A short list of known repairs. We buy as-is, but honest information avoids surprises.

Listing, selling it yourself or a cash offer: how they compare

Listing with an agent can bring a higher headline price when a house is in good shape and you have time. You pay the commission agreed in your listing contract, and you usually handle repairs, showings and the buyer's inspection requests. Closing depends on the buyer's financing.

Selling it yourself saves the listing commission but puts the marketing, the paperwork and the required Texas disclosures on you. You still need a title company or attorney to close.

Taking a cash offer trades some of the headline price for speed and certainty. We buy as-is, so there are no repairs, no showings and no financing contingency. It tends to fit owners dealing with foreclosure pressure, an inherited house, back taxes, tenants or a move on a deadline. Compare every option on what you net after repairs, fees and carrying costs, not on the headline price.

Questions to ask before you sell in Katy

  • Ask the tax collector what is owed and what the title company will need at closing.
  • Ask your lender for a written payoff figure good through your expected closing date, and ask whether there is a prepayment penalty.
  • Ask the county assessor whether a pending appeal or exemption affects the bill, and whether any exemption you receive ends when you sell.
  • If the house was inherited, ask the title company which court documents it needs before it will insure the sale.
  • If tenants live in the house, check the lease for its end date and any notice you must give.

These are general questions to start a conversation, not legal advice. Rules in Texas change, so confirm details with the official office or a Texas attorney or tax professional.

More questions about selling in Katy

How fast can I close on a cash sale?

You choose the closing date within what the title company needs to clear ownership and payoffs.

Do I have to clean out or repair the house?

No. We buy houses as-is, so you do not need to make repairs before selling.

Will you buy a house that has tenants in it?

Yes. We buy rentals as-is, occupied or vacant. Tell us about the lease when you request an offer.

What if I owe more on the mortgage than the house is worth?

Tell us the payoff figure. A sale that does not cover the loan may need lender approval, so ask your lender about a short sale before you sign anything.

Can I sell an inherited house before probate is finished?

It depends on who has legal authority to sign. The title company can tell you what court paperwork it needs.

Is there any cost to request an offer?

No. Requesting an offer is free and carries no obligation.

Katy property tax FAQ

When are Katy property taxes due?

January 31 of the year after the tax year. The 2026 bill is due Monday, February 1, 2027 because January 31 falls on a Sunday (Tax Code Secs. 31.02 and 1.06).

What is the penalty for paying late?

7 percent in February, rising to 18 percent by July, plus up to 20 percent in attorney fees after June 30 (Secs. 33.01 and 33.07).

How do I lower my property tax?

Claim the homestead exemption if you qualify and file a protest by May 15 or 30 days after the notice was delivered (Secs. 11.13 and 41.44).

Can I sell my Katy house if I owe property taxes?

Yes. The title company pays the taxes from your proceeds at closing.
